passages.text: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Maskil of David.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
David gave instructions to the choirmaster.
The choirmaster should use stringed instruments.
This psalm is a Maskil.
A Maskil is a type of contemplative or instructive song.

passages.text: Listen to my prayer, O God, and do not ignore my plea.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
He gave it to the choirmaster.
He wanted it played with stringed instruments.
David prayed to God.
He said, “God, listen to my prayer.”
He said, “Do not ignore my plea.”
passages.original: לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ בִּנְגִינֹ֗ת מַשְׂכִּ֥יל לְדָוִֽד׃ הַאֲזִ֣ינָה אֱ֭לֹהִים תְּפִלָּתִ֑י וְאַל־ תִּ֝תְעַלַּ֗ם מִתְּחִנָּתִֽי׃

passages.text: Attend to me and answer me. I am restless in my complaint, and distraught at the voice of the enemy, at the pressure of the wicked. For they release disaster upon me and revile me in their anger.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this prayer.
David speaks to God.
David says, "Attend to me."
David says, "Answer me."
David feels restless.
David complains.
David feels troubled.
David hears the enemy's voice.
David feels pressure from wicked people.
The wicked bring disaster upon David.
The wicked attack David in anger.
The wicked speak against David.
passages.original: הַקְשִׁ֣יבָה לִּ֣י וַעֲנֵ֑נִי אָרִ֖יד בְּשִׂיחִ֣י וְאָהִֽימָה׃ מִקּ֤וֹל אוֹיֵ֗ב מִפְּנֵ֣י עָקַ֣ת רָשָׁ֑ע כִּי־ יָמִ֥יטוּ עָלַ֥י אָ֝֗וֶן וּבְאַ֥ף יִשְׂטְמֽוּנִי׃

passages.text: My heart murmurs within me, and the terrors of death assail me.
passages.sermon:
David speaks these words in prayer to God.
David feels deep distress inside himself.
His heart trembles within him.
He feels the terrors of death fall upon him.
He is overwhelmed by fear.
passages.original: לִ֭בִּי יָחִ֣יל בְּקִרְבִּ֑י וְאֵימ֥וֹת מָ֝֗וֶת נָפְל֥וּ עָלָֽי׃

passages.text: Fear and trembling grip me, and horror has overwhelmed me.
passages.sermon: Fear comes to me.\r\nTrembling enters me.\r\nHorror covers me completely.
passages.original: יִרְאָ֣ה וָ֭רַעַד יָ֣בֹא בִ֑י וַ֝תְּכַסֵּ֗נִי פַּלָּצֽוּת׃

passages.text: I said, “Oh, that I had wings like a dove! I would fly away and find rest.
passages.sermon:
David speaks in deep distress.
He feels overwhelmed by fear and sorrow.
David longs to escape his troubles.
He says, “If only I had wings like a dove.
I would fly away from this place.
I would find a place to rest.”
passages.original: וָאֹמַ֗ר מִֽי־ יִתֶּן־ לִּ֣י אֵ֭בֶר כַּיּוֹנָ֗ה אָע֥וּפָה וְאֶשְׁכֹּֽנָה׃

passages.text: How far away I would flee! In the wilderness I would remain. Selah I would hurry to my shelter, far from this raging tempest.”
passages.sermon:
The speaker feels fear and horror.
The speaker wants to escape.
The speaker says, “I would flee far away.”
The speaker wants to stay in the wilderness.
The speaker says, “I would remain there.”
The speaker wants safety.
The speaker says, “I would hurry to my shelter.”
The speaker wants to be far from the storm.
The speaker says, “I would be far from this raging tempest.”
passages.original: הִ֭נֵּה אַרְחִ֣יק נְדֹ֑ד אָלִ֖ין בַּמִּדְבָּ֣ר סֶֽלָה׃ אָחִ֣ישָׁה מִפְלָ֣ט לִ֑י מֵר֖וּחַ סֹעָ֣ה מִסָּֽעַר׃

passages.text: O Lord, confuse and confound their speech, for I see violence and strife in the city.
passages.sermon:
The speaker prays to the Lord.
The speaker asks the Lord to confuse their speech.
The speaker asks the Lord to divide their language.
The speaker sees violence in the city.
The speaker sees strife in the city.
passages.original: בַּלַּ֣ע אֲ֭דֹנָי פַּלַּ֣ג לְשׁוֹנָ֑ם כִּֽי־ רָאִ֨יתִי חָמָ֖ס וְרִ֣יב בָּעִֽיר׃

passages.text: Day and night they encircle the walls, while malice and trouble lie within.
passages.sermon:
The city is full of violence and strife.
Day and night, people surround its walls.
Inside the city, there is malice.
Inside the city, there is trouble.
passages.original: יוֹמָ֤ם וָלַ֗יְלָה יְסוֹבְבֻ֥הָ עַל־ חוֹמֹתֶ֑יהָ וְאָ֖וֶן וְעָמָ֣ל בְּקִרְבָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: Destruction is within; oppression and deceit never leave the streets.
passages.sermon:
The city contains destruction.
Oppression fills the city.
Deceit fills the city.
Oppression never leaves the streets.
Deceit never leaves the streets.
passages.original: הַוּ֥וֹת בְּקִרְבָּ֑הּ וְֽלֹא־ יָמִ֥ישׁ מֵ֝רְחֹבָ֗הּ תֹּ֣ךְ וּמִרְמָֽה׃

passages.text: For it is not an enemy who insults me; that I could endure. It is not a foe who rises against me; from him I could hide.
passages.sermon:
The person speaking is not being insulted by an enemy.
An enemy is not the one who taunts him.
He could endure insults from an enemy.
A foe is not the one who rises against him.
He could hide from a foe.
passages.original: כִּ֤י לֹֽא־ אוֹיֵ֥ב יְחָֽרְפֵ֗נִי וְאֶ֫שָּׂ֥א לֹֽא־ מְ֭שַׂנְאִי עָלַ֣י הִגְדִּ֑יל וְאֶסָּתֵ֥ר מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: But it is you, a man like myself, my companion and close friend.
passages.sermon:
You are a man like me.
You are my companion.
You are my close friend.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֣ה אֱנ֣וֹשׁ כְּעֶרְכִּ֑י אַ֝לּוּפִ֗י וּמְיֻדָּֽעִי׃

passages.text: We shared sweet fellowship together; we walked with the crowd into the house of God.
passages.sermon:
We were close friends.
We shared secrets with each other.
We enjoyed good times together.
We went together into the house of God.
We walked with many others into God’s house.
We felt joy as we entered God’s house together.
passages.original: אֲשֶׁ֣ר יַ֭חְדָּו נַמְתִּ֣יק ס֑וֹד בְּבֵ֥ית אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים נְהַלֵּ֥ךְ בְּרָֽגֶשׁ׃

passages.text: Let death seize them by surprise; let them go down to Sheol alive, for evil is with them in their homes.
passages.sermon:
The psalmist speaks about his enemies.
He asks that death will come upon them suddenly.
He wants them to go down alive into Sheol, the place of the dead.
He says evil lives among them.
He says evil is in their homes.
passages.original: יַשִּׁימָוֶת עָלֵ֗ימוֹ יֵרְד֣וּ שְׁא֣וֹל חַיִּ֑ים כִּֽי־ רָע֖וֹת בִּמְגוּרָ֣ם בְּקִרְבָּֽם׃

passages.text: But I call to God, and the LORD saves me.
passages.sermon: I call to God.\r\nThe LORD saves me.
passages.original: אֲ֭נִי אֶל־ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֶקְרָ֑א וַ֝יהוָ֗ה יוֹשִׁיעֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: Morning, noon, and night, I cry out in distress, and He hears my voice.
passages.sermon:
David is the speaker.
David prays to God.
David speaks to God in the evening.
David speaks to God in the morning.
David speaks to God at noon.
David cries out to God when he is troubled.
God hears David’s voice.
passages.original: עֶ֤רֶב וָבֹ֣קֶר וְ֭צָהֳרַיִם אָשִׂ֣יחָה וְאֶהֱמֶ֑ה וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע קוֹלִֽי׃

passages.text: He redeems my soul in peace from the battle waged against me, even though many oppose me.
passages.sermon:
God redeems my soul.
He gives me peace.
He saves me from the battle against me.
Many people oppose me.
God is with me.
God rescues me.
passages.original: פָּ֘דָ֤ה בְשָׁל֣וֹם נַ֭פְשִׁי מִקֲּרָב־ לִ֑י כִּֽי־ בְ֝רַבִּ֗ים הָי֥וּ עִמָּדִֽי׃

passages.text: God will hear and humiliate them— the One enthroned for the ages— Selah because they do not change and they have no fear of God.
passages.sermon:
God sits on His throne forever.
God rules for all ages.
God hears them.
God answers them.
God will humble them.
They do not change their ways.
They do not fear God.
passages.original: יִשְׁמַ֤ע׀ אֵ֨ל׀ וְֽיַעֲנֵם֮ וְיֹ֤שֵׁ֥ב קֶ֗דֶם סֶ֥לָה אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֵ֣ין חֲלִיפ֣וֹת לָ֑מוֹ וְלֹ֖א יָרְא֣וּ אֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: My companion attacks his friends; he violates his covenant.
passages.sermon: My companion acts against his friends.\r\nHe breaks his promise to them.\r\nHe does not keep his covenant.
passages.original: שָׁלַ֣ח יָ֭דָיו בִּשְׁלֹמָ֗יו חִלֵּ֥ל בְּרִיתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: His speech is smooth as butter, but war is in his heart. His words are softer than oil, yet they are swords unsheathed.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm when the Philistines seized him in Gath.
David describes a companion.
This companion speaks with smooth words.
His speech is as smooth as butter.
But his heart is full of war.
His words are softer than oil.
But his words are actually like unsheathed swords.
passages.original: חָלְק֤וּ׀ מַחְמָאֹ֣ת פִּיו֮ וּֽקֲרָב־ לִ֫בּ֥וֹ רַכּ֖וּ דְבָרָ֥יו מִשֶּׁ֗מֶן וְהֵ֣מָּה פְתִחֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Cast your burden upon the LORD and He will sustain you; He will never let the righteous be shaken.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
God cares for His people.
Give your burden to the LORD.
God will support you.
God will not let the righteous fall.
God keeps the righteous safe forever.
passages.original: הַשְׁלֵ֤ךְ עַל־ יְהוָ֨ה׀ יְהָבְךָ֮ וְה֪וּא יְכַ֫לְכְּלֶ֥ךָ לֹא־ יִתֵּ֖ן לְעוֹלָ֥ם מ֗וֹט לַצַּדִּֽיק׃

passages.text: But You, O God, will bring them down to the Pit of destruction; men of bloodshed and deceit will not live out half their days. But I will trust in You.
passages.sermon:
God, You act with power and justice.
You will bring down the wicked.
You will send them to the Pit of destruction.
These wicked people are violent.
They shed blood.
They use deceit.
They will not live out half their days.
But I trust in You, God.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֤ה אֱלֹהִ֨ים׀ תּוֹרִדֵ֬ם׀ לִבְאֵ֬ר שַׁ֗חַת אַנְשֵׁ֤י דָמִ֣ים וּ֭מִרְמָה לֹא־ יֶחֱצ֣וּ יְמֵיהֶ֑ם וַ֝אֲנִ֗י אֶבְטַח־ בָּֽךְ׃
